slides.title: Talking the door open
slides.text: Most attacks never break a lock. They use facts you already made public, like your name, school and daily route, and talk you into opening the door.
slides.alt: The Fan Club post, binned: everything it knew came from a public profile. Flattery built from your footprint.

focus.cue: Facts made public: skateboards, a dog, a birthday
The door was talked open, not broken

slides.title: Four pressure levers
slides.text: A faked sender name can carry all four levers: authority, urgency, kindness and fear. Each lever pushes you to act before you stop and think.
slides.alt: Trick Inbox, Pressure: a letter says this is the head teacher speaking. Send your key before lunch, no questions.

focus.cue: Authority: this is the head teacher speaking

slides.title: A made-up reason
slides.text: A pretext is a made-up reason that makes a strange request sound normal. It might borrow a real event, like a lost bag, to explain why help is needed fast.
slides.alt: A Package Service letter: we could not deliver your package, pay a small fee within two hours.

focus.cue: A made-up reason: a package that never arrived
Then the ask: a fee, fast

slides.title: Check another way
slides.text: One move defeats every lever: verify through a different channel. Ask the person in real life, or type the real address yourself instead of tapping the link you were sent.
slides.alt: The head teacher letter, reported: authority is a costume here, and do not ask questions is the loudest clue.

slides.title: The Magpie asks nicely
slides.text: Last week the Magpie tried a new trick: no fake letters, just friendly questions about Pim's route. The clue was the pattern: every question fished for a private fact.
slides.alt: A Fun Quiz in game chat asks for your first pet, the street you grew up on and your birthday, then a share.

focus.cue: Friendly questions that fish for private facts

words.means: tricking people into giving away information
a made-up reason given to make a request seem safe
a push to act fast, before you can stop and think
to check, another way, that a claim is really true

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox at Pressure and sort all 6 messages. For each one, name the pressure lever pushing you before you choose.
slides.alt: A Shop Bot letter: only two left at this price, pay in the next five minutes or lose them forever.

focus.cue: Play Pressure: name the lever before you choose
